items.title: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
items.summary: Rio Tinto is ploughing millions of dollars into stopping the poisonous cane toad reaching the Pilbara region of western Australia, where the mining giant has a vast iron ore operation The firm, alongside Curtin University in Perth and others, will spend A$28m (£14.5m) building a "toad containment zone" to prevent the pest travelling south While the cane toad is not a direct threat to Rio Tinto's business, it produces toxins lethal to native wildlife and poses a threat to Pilbara's ecosystem Rio Tinto has previously faced criticism for destroying two sacred Aboriginal rock shelters in Pilbara which sat above tonnes of iron ore The decision cost the former chief executive his job, provoked a widespread backlash and saw Rio Tinto commit to rebuilding trust with Indigenous communities Commenting on the proposed containment zone, Roberta Hunter, a ranger in Australia's Nyangumarta Warrarn Indigenous Protected Area, said: "Cane toads destroy the water and animals "When toads come close to our country, we want to be there to stop them because we don't want the country to be destroyed." items.title: Mozambique and Malawi strengthen cooperation in defense and security
items.summary: Maputo, 03 Nov (AIM) – The governments of Mozambique and Malawi are adopting measures aimed at strengthening cooperation mechanisms in the fields of defense and security in order to prevent and fight against cross-border threats, including human and drug trafficking, illegal immigration, smuggling, and other forms of organized crime. The measures are being discussed in the 17th Session of the Joint Permanent Commission on Defense and Security (JPCDS), which started on Monday and closes on Wednesday, in Malawian city of Blantyre. According to Casimiro Mueio, Permanent Secretary of Mozambique’s Ministry of National Defense, there is a need to accelerate the implementation of decisions reached during the previous session held in Maputo in July 2025. He explained that information sharing and strengthened migration control is crucial to preventing human trafficking and locating missing minors. items.title: UK's King Charles III decries 'monstrous injustice' of slave trade
items.summary: King Charles has told leaders at a Commonwealth summit that the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade "fills my heart with horror." He did not address calls for apologies and reparations The United Kingdom 's King Charles III on Tuesday opened this week's Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda , a summit of 56 Commonwealth member-state leaders, by speaking of the tragic legacy of the transatlantic slave trade Charles told those gathered that he had furthered his "own understanding of the issues through listening, learning and looking." "The ​transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth. As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with ⁠horror ​and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow." The monarch stopped short of apologizing for Britain's role in the dark trade, as well as refraining from any talk of reparations .

items.title: Agricultural Campaign Plan budgeted at 189.8 million dollars launched

items.title: Uganda arrests former army deputy chief stripped of military rank
items.summary: Uganda accuses Peter Elwelu of stockpiling weapons and organising activities against the government Uganda has arrested former deputy military chief and presidential adviser Peter Elwelu over allegations of involvement in activities aimed at destabilising the country Acting military spokesman Chris Magezi said Elwelu, whom he described as a "renegade" officer, was arrested on Monday evening and would be charged in court The arrest comes days after Uganda's defence chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, announced that he had stripped Elwelu of his lieutenant general rank and demoted him to a private Elwelu has not commented on the allegations Elwelu rose to prominence in 2016 when he oversaw a deadly military raid on the palace of a regional king accused of leading a separatist movement. He was subsequently appointed army chief He later rose to become the deputy chief of defence forces before being named presidential adviser In May 2024, the US government imposed sanctions on him over alleged human rights abuses, including extrajudicial killings committed by government forces.
